claim: applications/react--performance.md's headline claim about goat - a runtime-selected rung ladder - is no longer true of the repo it cites; the Collection panel's decision site was deleted and the config, both predicates and the intersection trigger are now all dead.
because: CollectionPanel.tsx:95 is now `const displayItems = filteredItems;` with no predicate import (:1-21) and no LazyLoadTrigger render site; hooks/useCollectionLazyLoad.ts no longer exists in git ls-files; LazyLoadTrigger.tsx survives only as a barrel re-export at Collection/index.ts:15. The application's negative half (shouldUseVirtualization has no call site, src/lib/virtual/'s six modules unreferenced, two modules exporting one name at thresholds 20 and 50, docs/lazy-loading-implementation.md:18-22 documenting code that never ran) all still verify, and its line numbers in VirtualizedCollectionGrid.tsx have drifted by ~18.

claim: table/performance rung 3 names index KEYS as the memoization-defeater but not index PROPS, and a positional prop inside a memo comparator defeats memoization under exactly the operation memoization exists to survive.
because: ConfigurableCollectionItem.tsx:673 compares prevProps.index === nextProps.index inside its React.memo comparator, and index is consumed only for entrance-animation stagger (:576, :603). Every card below an insertion, deletion or resort therefore re-renders for a value that only offsets an animation which has already played - a rung-3 regression that passes the technique's stated 'key by identity, never by index' check because the keys ARE identities (CollectionPanel.tsx:279).

claim: The performance ladder is not monotonic: a surface can hold rung 3 while having abandoned rungs 1 and 4, so 'which rung is this on' is not answerable by one number and the technique's climb-only framing hides the regression.
because: In goat's Collection panel rung 1 and rung 4 were both removed (CollectionPanel.tsx:95 renders the whole filtered array) in the same period that rung 3 was built out: CollectionPanel.tsx:61-70 hoists four store subscriptions out of the rows with the reasoning written in the comment ('200 items x 4 stores = 800 subscriptions'), VirtualizedCollectionGrid.tsx:53-58 repeats the hoist, and ConfigurableCollectionItem.tsx:662-685 memoizes on the hoisted object. That is rung 3's 'rows read their own state; containers pass identity' realized exactly, on a surface that now mounts every row.

claim: The "exactly one resolver" rule survives a deprecation notice only on paper. A @deprecated reader with live call sites is still a resolver, so the audit unit the technique needs is "how many modules can answer the preference", not "which one is canonical" - and the canonical resolver existing is what makes the fan-out invisible, because every review of the right module comes back clean.
because: goat has exactly the resolver this technique describes - src/hooks/use-motion-preference.ts:279 merges the system query with an in-app tier, subscribes live, and depends on no engine - and three media-query-only readers still in service beside it: src/lib/animations/motion-presets.ts:112, src/lib/animations/micro-interactions.ts:58, src/app/features/Match/sub_MatchGrid/lib/hapticFeedback.ts:181. A fourth, src/hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts:40, carries an @deprecated notice naming the correct resolver and still has four live call sites (CollectionsSection.tsx:29, SectionHeader.tsx:42, UserListsSection.tsx:32, NeonArenaBackground.tsx:238). The consequence is exact and user-visible: a user who sets the in-app tier to "minimal" still gets full springs on every surface reached through those readers. The repo found this once and fixed it in one component only - the comment at src/components/visual/RankingProgressLayer.tsx:85 records the diagnosis - which is the shape of the failure: found per surface, never per product.

claim: "The signal has one subscription, not one per consumer" cannot be followed at the idiomatic hook layer on React: useSyncExternalStore calls subscribe once per component instance by construction, so a correct merged signal read through it still produces one platform listener per consumer. The fan-out has to be module-scoped BELOW the hook, and the half-built form - a module-level listener set that still attaches platform listeners inside each subscribe - reads as the technique satisfied.
because: goat builds the merged signal the technique asks for: src/hooks/use-animation-pause.ts:146 merges three enumerated deciders (page visibility, in-view, motion tier, listed at :110-113) into one shouldAnimate that five consumers read. But it is delivered by useSyncExternalStore, so each consumer runs src/hooks/use-animation-pause.ts:13 and adds its own visibilitychange listener. src/hooks/use-motion-preference.ts:54 shows the half-built fix: a module-level listeners Set exists, yet each subscribe call still adds a storage listener, a custom-event listener and a matchMedia listener (:73-75), so N consumers produce 3N platform listeners rather than three. The technique currently states the rule as an architecture property; on this framework it needs to state where the single subscription lives relative to the framework primitive, or the rule reads as satisfied by the module-level set alone.
